history.heading: Bantu peoples and Swahili trade
paragraphs: Bantu-speaking peoples settled present-day Mozambique around the first centuries CE. Coastal towns traded with Arab, Persian and Indian merchants, forming part of the Swahili world, and the inland Mutapa kingdom controlled gold trade routes.

Vasco da Gama reached the coast in 1498, and Portugal established trading posts, including on Mozambique Island, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mozambique became a source of enslaved people and later of forced labour for Portuguese companies and South African mines.

history.heading: Independence and civil war
paragraphs: The Liberation Front of Mozambique (FRELIMO), led by Eduardo Mondlane and later Samora Machel, began an armed struggle in 1964. After the 1974 revolution in Portugal, Mozambique became independent on 25 June 1975, with FRELIMO establishing a Marxist one-party state.
A civil war against RENAMO, backed by Rhodesia and apartheid South Africa, lasted from 1977 to 1992 and killed around a million people. Peace accords in 1992 led to multiparty elections in 1994.

history.heading: Recent decades
paragraphs: Mozambique grew quickly after the war but was hit by a hidden debt scandal in 2016. Since 2017 an Islamist insurgency in the northern province of Cabo Delgado has killed thousands and displaced around a million people; Rwandan and regional troops have deployed to help. Disputed elections in 2024 led to deadly protests.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Portuguese is the official language, and many Bantu languages, such as Makhuwa, Sena and Tsonga, are widely spoken. Most people are Christian, with a large Muslim population in the north.

Timbila music of the Chopi people and Makonde wood carving are renowned. Marrabenta is popular urban music. Mozambican cuisine includes peri-peri chicken, matapa (cassava leaves) and seafood. Athlete Maria Mutola won Olympic gold in 2000.

politics.heading: Presidential republic
paragraphs: Mozambique is a presidential republic. FRELIMO has governed continuously since independence. Daniel Chapo was declared winner of the 2024 election, which the opposition and observers criticised. Corruption and the northern insurgency are major issues.

economy.heading: Resources and poverty
paragraphs: Mozambique is one of the poorest countries in the world, with most people relying on subsistence farming. It has large natural gas reserves off Cabo Delgado, with major LNG projects, though some were delayed by the insurgency. Aluminium smelting, coal, rubies and graphite are important exports.
Cyclones, such as Idai in 2019, and floods cause frequent devastation. The currency is the metical.
